title: Unsafe Abstraction Drop and Panic Safety
platform_conditions: Any Rust toolchain; drop/panic interaction semantics are toolchain-independent, Pin projection rules apply to async/future types
security_mechanism: Rust's safety story assumes every value is dropped exactly once and destructors always run, but unsafe abstractions can break both. ptr::read copies the value out bitwise while leaving the source intact: if the source is later dropped normally, the same value is dropped twice, and if a panic fires between read and forget the double drop happens mid-unwind. Abstractions that rely on the destructor to restore an invariant (releasing a lock, decrementing a count, restoring a file mode) leave the invariant broken if a panic skips the drop path they assumed — unwinding still runs destructors, but only for values already constructed, so ManuallyDrop/DontDrop fields and manually-managed slots escape cleanup. Pin misuse (moving a pinned value, or projecting a non-structural field as structural) breaks self-referential futures whose internal pointers then dangle across the next poll.

source_sink_clues.source: Attacker-triggerable panics and early returns that interrupt an unsafe abstraction between its setup and teardown steps (parse errors mid-construction, request cancellation between polls).
source_sink_clues.sink: unsafe { ptr::read / ptr::copy_nonoverlapping } followed by manual mem::forget; Drop implementations assuming they always run; Pin projections that move pinned data; invariants restored only in explicit (not drop-guard) code paths

tracking_guards: Check that every ptr::read is paired with mem::forget or ManuallyDrop on ALL paths including panic unwinding, that resource-releasing and invariant-restoring logic lives in Drop rather than a call the caller may skip, and that Pin projections follow the pinned-field rules (structural pinning only for fields that are genuinely pinned).
not_candidate_when: The read/forget pair is total on every path and the type is UnwindSafe-verified, invariants are enforced by Drop guards so unwinding restores them, the pinned type has no structural self-references (Pin is only a marker there), or the abstraction is unreachable from input-triggered panics.
